--- title: "Results: Critiques & Key Issues" engine: knitr execute: freeze: auto --- ::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"} Detailed paper-by-paper critique comparisons (matched issue pairs, severity labels, structural differences) are available in the online supplement at . ::: ::: {.content-visible when-format="html"} ::: {.cell} ::: []{#critique-headline} ::: {.callout-tip} ## Headline result: overlap between model and expert critiques (n = 12 papers) **Coverage: between about 44% and 80%, depending on the judge (see below).** The figures that follow are from the original judge. **Original judge, coverage: 80%.** For each paper we compared the key issues in the one-shot GPT-5.2 Pro report with the curated human consensus issues: the concerns that the evaluation manager judged most important across the human evaluations. On average the model raised 80% of those human issues (range across papers 50–100%). **LLM overlap rate: 52%.** On average, 52% of the issues the model raised matched a concern on the curated human list (range 17–83%). **Raw counts, pooled over the 12 papers.** The curated human lists contain 63 issues: the model matched 53 and missed 10. The model raised 142 issues: 73 matched a human concern and 69 did not. The headline percentages are averages of per-paper rates, so they differ slightly from these pooled ratios (84% and 51%). **What the unmatched model issues mean.** We have not yet checked the 69 unmatched model issues. Some are probably valid points that the human evaluators did not raise or that did not make the curated list; others may be wrong, minor, or repetitive. An unmatched issue is not, by itself, an error. **A stricter judge gives lower figures.** We re-judged the same 12 papers with a revised, blinded judge (November 2026). Both issue lists were first rewritten into neutral statements so the judge could not tell which was human; a different model (Claude Opus 5.5) then classified each pair by whether it concerns the same result and the same reason for criticising it. Coverage then depends on what counts as a match: | What counts as a match | Coverage of human issues | Model issues matched | |---|---:|---:| | Original judge (GPT-5.2 Pro, 0–100 score, 30 or more) | 80% | 52% | | Revised judge: same concern | 28% | 10% | | Revised judge: same concern, possibly broader or narrower | 44% | 17% | | Revised judge: also the same result criticised for a different reason | 64% | 34% | : Mean per-paper rates. Revised-judge rates average two runs. {.striped} In 8 control cases that paired critiques of *different* papers, the revised judge found no matches at any level (maximum coverage 0%), so chance matches are rare under its rubric. Its two runs agreed on whether each human issue was covered for 51 of 54 issues. Spot checks suggest the original judge was generous: it credited a match on data leakage to model points that do not mention leakage. They also suggest the revised judge can be strict, when both sides question the same confidence intervals for different reasons. **Until human annotators check the borderline pairs, we treat the overlap as uncertain, somewhere between about 44% and 80%.** Details: [revised-judge note](https://github.com/valentinklotzbuecher/llm-uj-research-eval/blob/working-paper/docs/issue_match_judge_v2_pilot_2026-11-10.md). **Short version to quote:** "In 12 eligible papers, the one-shot GPT-5.2 Pro reports raised on average 80% of the curated human consensus issues (range 50 to 100%), and on average 52% of the issues the model raised matched one of those human concerns. A stricter, blinded re-judging of the same 12 papers gives lower overlap: 44% coverage when only the same concern counts, 64% at a loose level that also counts criticism of the same result for a different reason." **Caveats.** - The original matches were judged by GPT-5.2 Pro, the same model that wrote the critiques. The revised judge uses a different model and blinding but has not yet been checked against human annotators; that check is the next step. - The revised judge splits the human critiques into 54 items, against 63 in the original run, so per-paper rates are not exactly comparable. - 12 papers, so this is exploratory. Two of the 14 original pairings are excluded because the human and model critiques concern different manuscripts (see *Data sources* below). - The human reference is the curated consensus list, not every point raised by individual evaluators. - The separate Claude Opus 5.5 [persistent-misses diagnostic](persistent_misses.qmd) is not pooled with these numbers. The [per-paper figure](#fig-coverage-precision) below shows how the original judge's coverage and overlap vary across papers. Every judged pair, with the judge's explanation, is in the repository: `results/key_issues_comparison_results.json` (original) and `results/issue_match_judge_v2_opus55_2026-11-10/` (revised). ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Setup and libraries"} source("scripts/analysis_checks.R") library("tidyverse") library("jsonlite") library("knitr") library("kableExtra") library("DT") library("reticulate") # Theme colors — crisp palette (matching results.qmd) UJ_ORANGE <- "#E8722A" # vivid saffron orange UJ_GREEN <- "#2D9D5E" # rich emerald green UJ_BLUE <- "#2B7CE9" # clear azure blue # Severity colors for badges SEV_NECESSARY <- "#D62839" # Bright crimson SEV_OPTIONAL <- "#E8722A" # Saffron orange SEV_UNSURE <- "#8B95A2" # Cool grey theme_uj <- function(base_size = 12) { theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey88"), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.1)), plot.title.position = "plot", plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = rel(0.9)), plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey50", size = rel(0.8), hjust = 0), axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.95)), axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.88)), legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.88)), legend.title = element_text(size = rel(0.9), face = "bold"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.95)) ) } # Function to create severity badge HTML severity_badge <- function(severity) { sev <- tolower(trimws(severity)) if (grepl("necessary", sev)) { return('Necessary') } else if (grepl("optional", sev)) { return('Optional') } else if (sev != "") { return('Unsure') } return('\u2014') } # Function to truncate text for table display truncate_text <- function(text, max_chars = 80) { if (nchar(text) > max_chars) { paste0(substr(text, 1, max_chars), "...") } else { text } } ``` ::: This chapter reports preliminary results from comparing LLM-identified key issues against human expert critiques. The analysis uses LLM-based assessment (GPT-5.2 Pro as judge) to measure human-issue coverage and the LLM overlap rate; human validation of these alignment scores is underway. ::: {.callout-note} ## Follow-up: do the misses persist? A separate, provisional diagnostic re-tested several critiques that the earlier models missed, using Claude Opus 5.5. It found that some misses no longer occur, some persist, and the model disputes three of the critiques. See [Persistent misses: a provisional Claude Opus 5.5 diagnostic](persistent_misses.qmd). Its scores await human review and are not pooled with the numbers on this page. ::: ::: {.callout-tip} ## Check the judges' matches The [issue match audit page](https://daaronr.github.io/unjournal_tools_interfaces/annotation/ui/audit.html) shows each human-to-model issue match that an AI judge proposed, for this 12-paper comparison and the November critique-overlap pilot, and asks a reviewer whether the two issues are the same, partly the same or different. It reports judge-to-judge, reviewer-to-judge and reviewer-to-reviewer agreement (Cohen's kappa). No reviewer verdicts have been collected yet, so the judges' precision against human review is still unknown. ::: **Data sources.** We compare GPT-5.2 Pro key issues (structured output from the focal evaluation run, January 2026) against human expert critiques curated from The Unjournal's internal tracking database, where evaluation managers synthesize evaluator feedback using severity labels ("Necessary", "Optional but important", "Unsure"). The focal run covered 14 papers. Two critique pairings are excluded: Peterman et al. 2025 (the human critique concerns a different manuscript) and Bénabou et al. 2023 (human critiques of *Willful Ignorance and Moral Behavior* paired with model critiques of *Ends versus Means: Kantians, Utilitarians, and Moral Decisions*). The exclusions are documented in `results/key_issues_comparison.md` and `docs/concordance_three_candidate_methods_note_jul2026.md`. A shared check excludes both keys before analysis, retaining the original responses for provenance. The resulting analysis covers 12 pairs; it remains exploratory pending an identity audit of the full corpus and independent human validation. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Load comparison data"} # Load the matched comparison data comparison_file <- "results/key_issues_comparison.json" comparison_results_file <- c( "results/key_issue_comp_results.json", "results/key_issues_comparison_results.json" ) comparison_results_file <- comparison_results_file[file.exists(comparison_results_file)][1] if (file.exists(comparison_file)) { comparison_data <- exclude_misaligned_critiques(fromJSON(comparison_file)) n_papers <- nrow(comparison_data) } else { comparison_data <- NULL n_papers <- 0 } # Load LLM-based comparison results if available. The legacy precision_pct # field is displayed as the LLM overlap rate. if (!is.null(comparison_data) && !is.na(comparison_results_file)) { llm_results_raw <- fromJSON(comparison_results_file) llm_results <- llm_results_raw |> as_tibble() |> unnest_wider(comparison) |> select( gpt_paper, coverage_pct, precision_pct, # New format uses matched_pairs, unmatched_human, unmatched_llm any_of(c("matched_pairs", "unmatched_human", "unmatched_llm")), # Old format used missed_issues, extra_issues (keep for backward compat) any_of(c("missed_issues", "extra_issues")), overall_rating, overall_justification, detailed_notes ) comparison_data <- comparison_data |> left_join(llm_results, by = "gpt_paper", relationship = "one-to-one") } # Update paper count after loading if (!is.null(comparison_data)) { n_papers <- nrow(comparison_data) } ``` ::: We matched **12 papers** with both GPT-5.2 Pro key issues and human expert critiques. **LLM-based assessment.** The comparison was assessed using GPT-5.2 Pro, which evaluated coverage (what proportion of human concerns GPT identified) and the LLM overlap rate (what proportion of LLM issues matched a curated human concern). - **Coverage**: Proportion of *consensus* human issues that have any LLM match (match quality >= 30%) - **Weighted Coverage**: Mean match quality across all human issues (treating unmatched issues as 0%) - **LLM overlap rate**: Proportion of LLM issues that match a curated human concern ::: callout-note ## Caveat on the LLM overlap rate The LLM overlap rate only reflects whether LLM issues match the *consensus* human issues curated in Coda---those prioritized by evaluation managers as the most important concerns. Many LLM-identified issues may have been noted by one or more individual human evaluators but were not included in this curated set. A low overlap rate does not mean the LLM raised irrelevant or incorrect concerns; it may simply reflect issues that were not prioritized in the consensus summary. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} # Check if LLM comparison results are available has_llm_results <- !is.null(comparison_data) && n_papers > 0 && "coverage_pct" %in% names(comparison_data) && any(!is.na(comparison_data$coverage_pct)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell tbl-cap='LLM assessment of GPT vs human critique alignment'} ```{.r .cell-code} if (has_llm_results) { # Filter to papers with valid LLM results llm_results <- comparison_data |> filter(!is.na(coverage_pct) & !is.na(precision_pct)) summary_stats <- llm_results |> summarise( `Papers Assessed` = n(), `Mean Coverage (%)` = round(mean(coverage_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1), `Mean LLM overlap rate (%)` = round(mean(precision_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1), `Coverage Range` = paste0(min(coverage_pct, na.rm = TRUE), "-", max(coverage_pct, na.rm = TRUE)), `LLM overlap-rate range` = paste0(min(precision_pct, na.rm = TRUE), "-", max(precision_pct, na.rm = TRUE)) ) |> mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") kable(summary_stats, align = c("l", "r")) } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Metric Value
Papers Assessed 12
Mean Coverage (%) 79.9
Mean LLM overlap rate (%) 51.5
Coverage Range 50-100
LLM overlap-rate range 17-83
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (has_llm_results) { llm_results <- comparison_data |> filter(!is.na(coverage_pct) & !is.na(precision_pct)) |> mutate(paper_short = str_trunc(gpt_paper, 25)) ggplot(llm_results, aes(x = coverage_pct, y = precision_pct)) + geom_point(size = 4.5, color = UJ_ORANGE, alpha = 0.85) + geom_text(aes(label = paper_short), hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.6, check_overlap = TRUE) + geom_vline(xintercept = mean(llm_results$coverage_pct), linetype = "dashed", color = UJ_BLUE, linewidth = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = mean(llm_results$precision_pct), linetype = "dashed", color = UJ_BLUE, linewidth = 0.6) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) + labs( x = "Coverage (%) \u2014 Human issues captured by LLM", y = "LLM overlap rate (%)" ) + theme_uj() } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Coverage (% of human-identified issues captured by the LLM) vs LLM overlap rate (% of LLM-raised issues matching a curated human concern), as assessed by GPT-5.2 Pro acting as judge. Each point is one paper. Dashed blue lines mark cross-paper means. Papers in the upper-right show strong human–LLM critique alignment.](results_critiques_files/figure-html/fig-coverage-precision-1.png){#fig-coverage-precision width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Interpretation Guide - **Coverage**: Percentage of human-identified issues that GPT also captured (in some form). Higher = GPT missed fewer human concerns. - **LLM overlap rate**: Percentage of GPT issues that match the curated human concern set. Higher means more overlap, but unmatched concerns are not necessarily incorrect. - **Overall Rating**: Qualitative assessment (Excellent/Good/Moderate/Poor) based on both coverage and overlap metrics. ::: The coverage-overlap figure above shows substantial variation across papers: some papers achieve high coverage and overlap, while others show the LLM missing key human concerns or raising issues not in the expert consensus. Paper-by-paper comparisons with matched issue pairs, structural difference tables, and the manual annotation tool are available in the [full online version](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/results_critiques.html). :::
